'''María Antonia Blasco Marhuenda''' (born 1965), known as '''María Blasco''', is a Spanish [[molecular biologist]]. She was the director of the [[Spanish National Cancer Research Centre]] (Centro Nacional de Investigaciones Oncológicas, CNIO) from June 22, 2011 to January 29, 2025.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Domínguez |first=Nuño |date=2025-01-29 |title=El patronato del CNIO destituye por unanimidad a la directora, María Blasco, y al gerente del centro |url=https://elpais.com/ciencia/2025-01-29/el-patronato-del-cnio-destituye-a-maria-blasco-y-al-gerente.html |access-date=2025-01-30 |website=El País |language=es}}</ref> Her research focuses on [[telomere]]s, [[telomerase]], and their relationship with [[aging]] and [[cancer]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ranf.com/sesion/toma-de-posesion-como-academica-de-numero-en-la-medalla-28-de-la-excma-sra-dna-maria-blasco-marhuenda/ |title=Toma de posesión como Académica de Número, en la Medalla 28, de la Excma. Sra. Dña. María Blasco Marhuenda |publisher=Real Academia Nacional de Farmacia |access-date=2024-12-15 |language=es}}</ref>

==Life==
Blasco was born in 1965. She graduated in Biological Sciences from the [[University of Valencia]] in 1988.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cnio.es/es/grupos/plantillas/curriculum.asp?pag=39 |title=CNIO web 2009 |access-date=2023-07-09 |archive-date=2009-01-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090115105230/http://www.cnio.es/es/grupos/plantillas/curriculum.asp?pag=39 |url-status=dead}}</ref> She obtained her PhD in 1993 for her research at the ''Centro de Biología Molecular Severo Ochoa'' ([[Autonomous University of Madrid|UAM]]-[[Spanish National Research Council|CSIC]]), under the supervision of [[Margarita Salas]]. Her doctoral thesis was titled ''Estudios de la relación estructura-función en DNA polimerasa DNA-dependiente del bacteriófago ø29''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://hdl.handle.net/10486/663366 |title=Estudios de la relación estructura-función en DNA polimerasa DNA-dependiente del bacteriofago ø29 |date=5 February 1993 |author=Blasco Marhuenda, María Antonia |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://dialnet.unirioja.es/servlet/tesis?codigo=140023 |title=Estudios de la relación estructura-función en DNA polimerasa DNA-dependiente del bacteriofago ø29 |last=Blasco |first=María A. |date=1993 |publisher=Universidad Autónoma de Madrid |access-date=2021-06-19 |language=es}}</ref> That same year, Blasco joined the [[Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory]] in New York (USA) as a Postdoctoral Fellow under the leadership of [[Carol W. Greider]] (who was to win a Nobel Prize in 2009). While there, Blasco cloned one of the genes for mammalian telomerase and generated the first [[knockout mouse]] for telomerase.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cnio.es/es/grupos/plantillas/curriculum.asp?pag=39 |title=CNIO web 2009 |access-date=2023-07-09 |archive-date=2009-01-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090115105230/http://www.cnio.es/es/grupos/plantillas/curriculum.asp?pag=39 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 1997, she returned to Spain to start her own research at the ''Centro Nacional de Biotecnología'' in Madrid. She worked there as a group leader and CSIC scientist in the Department of Immunology and Oncology.<ref>[http://www.uam.es/ss/Satellite/es/1242649910548/1242658643486/noticia/noticia/1242658643486.htm María Blasco, directora del Centro Nacional de Investigaciones Oncológicas (CNIO), Premio Antiguos Alumnos 2011], Universidad Autónoma de Madrid, 25 November 2011.</ref> She joined the ''Centro Nacional de Investigaciones Oncológicas (CNIO)'' in 2003 as Director of the Molecular Oncology Programme and Leader of the Telomeres and Telomerase Group.

In 2005, she was also assigned as Vice-Director of Basic Research, and, in 2011, she was appointed as CNIO Director, replacing [[Mariano Barbacid]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Biosketch: María A. Blasco at CNIO|url=https://www.cnio.es/es/grupos/plantillas/curriculum.asp?pag=39|publisher=CNIO|access-date=2014-05-22|archive-date=2018-09-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180908060409/https://www.cnio.es/ES/grupos/plantillas/curriculum.asp?pag=39|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=CNIOBlascoMarhuenda>[http://www.elpais.com/articulo/sociedad/investigadora/Maria/Blasco/sustituye/Barbacid/frente/CNIO/elpepusocsal/20110622elpepusoc_1/Tes La investigadora María Blasco sustituye a Barbacid al frente del CNIO, 22/6/2011] - [[El País]]</ref>

In 2010, Blasco co-founded [[Life Length]], a biotech company, along with entrepreneur Stephen J. Matlin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnio.es/|title= CNIO}}</ref> More recently, she founded the startup Telomere Therapeutics, initially with the aim of developing a telomerase-based [[gene therapy]] for [[pulmonary fibrosis]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cnio.es/noticias/noticias-cnio/spin-off-cnio-uab-terapia-genica-fibrosis-pulmonar/ |title=Una ''spin-off'' del CNIO y la UAB desarrollará una terapia génica para la fibrosis pulmonar |website=CNIO |language=es}}</ref>

In December 2024, 23 research group leaders at the CNIO called for Blasco's removal, criticizing her management and the resources available for basic research.<ref>{{cite news |last=Domínguez |first=Nuño |date=2024-12-16 |title=Científicos del CNIO, el mayor centro de cáncer de España, exigen al Gobierno que cese a María Blasco |url=https://elpais.com/ciencia/2024-12-16/cientificos-del-cnio-el-mayor-centro-de-cancer-de-espana-exigen-al-gobierno-que-cese-a-maria-blasco.html |work=El País |access-date=2024-12-17 |language=es}}</ref> Blasco said that responsibility for the CNIO's finances and contracting lay with its managing director, Juan Arroyo. She said that she shared researchers' concerns about insufficient resources and low salaries and announced her intention to seek an audit of the center from the [[Ombudsman of Spain]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Peco |first=Marina |date=2024-12-23 |title=La directora del CNIO, María Blasco, achaca las críticas a la gestión económica: "Yo no controlo las cuentas" |url=https://www.rtve.es/noticias/20241223/directora-cnio-achaca-criticas-gestion-economica/16383774.shtml |website=RTVE.es |access-date=2024-12-23 |language=es}}</ref> The CNIO board subsequently declined to approve the center's 2025 action plan, requested an "exhaustive explanation" of its situation, and suspended activities of the CNIO-Arte program.<ref>{{cite news |last=Domínguez |first=Nuño |date=2024-12-17 |title=El patronato tumba las cuentas de 2025 del CNIO, el mayor centro de cáncer de España, y exige una "explicación exhaustiva" a la dirección |url=https://elpais.com/ciencia/2024-12-17/el-gobierno-tumba-las-cuentas-de-2025-del-cnio-el-mayor-centro-de-cancer-de-espana-y-exige-una-explicacion-exhaustiva-a-la-direccion.html |work=El País |access-date=2024-12-19 |language=es}}</ref>

On January 29, 2025, the CNIO board dismissed both Blasco and Arroyo from their positions.<ref name=":0" /> In November 2025, ''[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]'' reported allegations that Arroyo had diverted more than €20 million through irregular contracts involving a network of companies connected to his circle.<ref>{{cite news |date=2025-11-16 |title=Un alto cargo del CNIO denuncia el robo de 25 millones de la lucha contra el cáncer en contratos públicos durante 18 años |url=https://www.elmundo.es/espana/2025/11/16/6919fa02fc6c8340188b4577.html |work=El Mundo |access-date=2025-12-05 |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=2025-11-25 |title=El CNIO destituye al ex gerente acusado del desfalco de 25 millones de la lucha contra el cáncer mediante contratos irregulares |url=https://www.elmundo.es/espana/2025/11/25/6925a5e1fc6c83d8388b45a1.html |work=El Mundo |access-date=2025-12-05 |language=es}}</ref> Blasco said that she had asked the CNIO board in 2022 to dismiss Arroyo and argued that she had been made a scapegoat for matters that were outside her responsibilities.<ref>{{cite news |date=2025-12-01 |title=María Blasco: "Pedí que echaran al gerente del CNIO: no hicieron nada y me cesaron a mí" |url=https://www.elmundo.es/espana/2025/12/01/692dfcf2fdddffd4308b4597.html |work=El Mundo |access-date=2025-12-05 |language=es}}</ref> In March 2026, she was named the Monte-Carlo Woman of the Year at the Monaco Women Forum.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://lagazettedemonaco.com/en/news/societe/prix-monte-carlo-femme-de-lannee-deux-scientifiques-primees-pour-leurs-recherches-sur-la-longevite-en|title=Monte-Carlo Woman of the Year Award: Two scientists honored for their longevity research|work=La Gazette de Monaco|date=24 March 2026}}</ref>

== Research ==

* Isolation of the core components of mouse [[telomerase]] and generation of the first knockout mouse for telomerase;<ref>{{cite journal|last=Blasco|first=MA|author2=Funk W |author3=Villaponteau B |author4=Greider CW |title=Functional characterization and developmental regulation of mouse telomerase RNA component.|journal=Science|year=1995|volume=269|issue=5228|pages=1267–1270 |doi=10.1126/science.7544492|pmid=7544492|s2cid=1315745 }}</ref> 
* Generation of the first mouse with increased telomerase expression in adult tissues;<ref>{{cite journal|last=Blasco|first=MA|author2=Lee H-W |author3=Hande P |author4=Samper E |author5=Lansdorp P |author6=DePinho R |author7=Greider CW |title=Telomere shortening and tumor formation by mouse cells lacking telomerase RNA.|journal=Cell|year=1997|volume=91|issue=1|pages=25–34 |doi=10.1016/s0092-8674(01)80006-4 |pmid=9335332|doi-access=free}}</ref> 
* The finding that mammalian telomeres and subtelomeres have epigenetic marks characteristic of constitutive heterochromatin;<ref>{{cite journal|last=Blasco|first=MA|author2=Garcia-Cao, M. |author3=O'Sullivan, R. |author4=Peters, A.H. |author5=Jenuwein, T. |title=Epigenetic regulation of telomere length in mammalian cells by the Suv39h1 and Suv39h2 histone methyltransferases|journal=Nature Genetics|year=2004|volume=36|pages=94–99 |doi=10.1038/ng1278 |issue=1|pmid=14702045 |doi-access=free}}</ref> 
* Discovery of telomeric RNAs, which are potent telomerase-inhibitors whose expression is altered in cancer;<ref>{{cite journal|last=Schoeftner, S.|author2=Blasco, MA|title=Developmentally regulated transcription of mammalian telomeres by DNA dependent RNA polymerase II|journal=Nature Cell Biology|year=2008|volume=10|pages=228–236|doi=10.1038/ncb1685|pmid=18157120|issue=2|s2cid=5890629 }}</ref>
* Demonstration that telomerase activity and telomere length determine the regenerative capacity of adult stem cells;<ref>{{cite journal|last=Benetti, R.|author2=García-Cao, M. |author3=Blasco, MA |title=Telomere length regulates the epigenetic status of mammalian telomeres and subtelomeres|journal=Nature Genetics|year=2007|volume=39|pages=243–250|doi=10.1038/ng1952|issue=2|pmid=17237781|s2cid=770312 }}</ref>
* Identification of the longest telomeres as a universal feature of adult stem cell niches;<ref>{{cite journal|last=Flores, I.|author2=Canela, A. |author3=Vera, E. |author4=Tejera, A. |author5=Cotsarelis, G. |author6=Blasco, MA |title=The longest telomeres: a general signature of adult stem cell compartments|journal=Genes & Development|year=2008|volume=22|issue=5 |pages=654–667 |doi=10.1101/gad.451008 |pmid=18283121 |pmc=2259034}}</ref>
* The finding that telomerase overexpression in the context of cancer resistant-mice improves organismal fitness, produces a systemic delay in ageing and an extension in median life-span;<ref>{{cite journal|last=Tomas, A. |author2=Flores, I. |author3=Fernandez-Marcos, P. |author4=Cayuela, M.L |author5=Maraver, A. |author6=Tejera, A. |author7=Borras, C. |author8=Matheu, A. |author9=Klatt, P. |author10=Flores, J.M. |author11=Viña, J. |author12=Serrano, M. |author13=Blasco, MA|title=Telomerase reverse transcriptase delays aging in cancer resistant mice|journal=Cell|volume=135|pages=609–622|doi=10.1016/j.cell.2008.09.034|pmid=19013273|issue=4|date=November 2008|doi-access=free }}</ref>
* Discovery that telomeres rejuvenate after nuclear reprogramming;
* Identification of the molecular mechanisms by which short telomeres/DNA damage limit nuclear reprogramming of defective cells;<ref>{{cite journal|last=arion, R.M.|author2=Strati, K. |author3=Li, H. |author4=Murga, M. |author5=Blanco, R. |author6=Ortega, S. |author7=Fernandez-Capetillo, O. |author8=Serrano, M. |author9=Blasco, MA |title=A p53-mediated DNA damage response limits reprogramming to ensure iPS cell genomic integrity.|journal=Nature|volume=460|pages=1149–1153 |doi=10.1038/nature08287 |pmid=19668189 |issue=7259 |date=August 2009 |pmc=3624089|bibcode=2009Natur.460.1149M }}</ref>
* Discovery that telomeric protein TRF1 can act as both a tumour suppressor and as a factor in ageing prevention.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Martinez, P.|author2=Thanasoula, M. |author3=Muñoz, P. |author4=Liao, C. |author5=Tejera, A. |author6=McNees, C. |author7=Flores, J.M. |author8=Fernández-Capetillo, O. |author9=Tarsounas, M. |author10=Blasco, MA |title=Increased telomere fragility and fusions resulting from TRF1 deficiency lead to degenerative pathologies and increased cancer in mice|journal=Genes Dev.|year=2009|volume=23|issue=17 |pages=2060–2075 |doi=10.1101/gad.543509 |pmid=19679647 |pmc=2751970}}</ref>

== Professional experience ==

* 2011– 2025 	Director [[Spanish National Cancer Research Centre]] (Centro Nacional de Investigaciones Oncológicas, CNIO)
* 2005–2011	Vice-Director of Basic Research (CNIO)
* 2003–2011	Director, Molecular Oncology Program (CNIO)
* 2003–present	Head, Telomeres and Telomerase Group (CNIO)
* 1997–2003	Staff Investigator, National Center of Biotechnology, Madrid, Spain
* 1993–1996	Postdoctoral Fellow, Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, New York, USA. supervisor Dr. Carol. W. Greider
* 1992–1993	Postoctoral Fellow, Center of Molecular Biology, Madrid, Spain. supervisor Dr. Margarita Salas
* 1989–1992       Graduate Fellow, Center of Molecular Biology, Madrid, Spain supervisor Dr. Margarita Salas
